items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted. The present study aimed to investigate the extent to which the effectiveness of a retraction is determined by its credibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada com cenários fictícios, atendendo ao critério de neutralidade. O estudo é empírico (dois experimentos), o método descrito é consistente com o resumo e o achado principal é sustentado pelo texto do resumo.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que o estudo é empírico (três estudos), trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e sustenta o achado de que o fornecimento de uma explicação alternativa reduziu o efeito.

items.title: The role of discomfort in the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Research examining the continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation has reliably found that belief in misinformation persists even after the misinformation has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Studies 1 and 2 found that retractions of misinformation elicit psychological discomfort, and this discomfort predicts continued belief in and use of misinformation. Study 3 showed that the relations between discomfort and continued belief in and use of misinformation are causal in nature by manipulating how participants appraised the meaning of discomfort.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e é um estudo empírico experimental. O resumo confirma que o estudo utilizou três experimentos para investigar o papel do desconforto no CIE. Embora o resumo não mencione explicitamente o cenário de 'incêndio em um galpão', o método experimental descrito no resumo é consistente com o que foi extraído.

items.title: The independent effects of source expertise and trustworthiness on retraction believability: The moderating role of vested interest

judge.evidence_topic: Study 1 demonstrated that retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source while controlling for perceptions of trustworthiness. Additionally, Study 1 demonstrated that this only occurs when the source had no vested interest in issuing the retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: Study 1 demonstrated that retractions from an expert source are believed more and lead to less continued belief in misinformation than retractions from an inexpert source while controlling for perceptions of trustworthiness. Study 2 found similar effects using a design containing manipulations of both expertise and trustworthiness.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com materiais neutros, publicado em periódico. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.reason: O artigo é empírico e trata do tema solicitado. O achado principal está sustentado pelo resumo. Contudo, a descrição do método na extração inclui 'incêndio em um galpão', informação que não consta no resumo fornecido, violando a regra de usar apenas as informações fornecidas.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com cenários fictícios, sendo um estudo empírico experimental. O método descrito (dois experimentos comparando tipos de correção) é consistente com o resumo. O achado principal de que explicar a origem da desinformação não torna a correção mais eficaz é sustentado pelo resumo: 'Overall, the results suggest that informing people of the cause leading to presentation of misinformation... may not be an effective correction strategy over and above stating that the misinformation is false.'

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE). Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários neutros (eventos), atendendo ao recorte do pedido. O estudo é empírico, baseado em dois experimentos. O método descrito no resumo (uso de limites de eventos para manipular a integração da retratação) é consistente com a descrição extraída. O achado principal extraído corresponde exatamente à conclusão apresentada no resumo sobre os resultados dos experimentos 1 e 2.

items.title: Listening to Misinformation while Driving: Cognitive Load and the Effectiveness of (Repeated) Corrections

judge.evidence_topic: Corrected misinformation can continue to influence inferential reasoning. Participants listened to corrections that repeated misinformation while in a driving simulator.
judge.evidence_empirical: We tested whether familiarity backfire may occur if corrections are processed under cognitive load. Participants listened to corrections that repeated misinformation while in a driving simulator.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que investiga o efeito de influência continuada em um contexto neutro (simulador de direção), atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O achado principal está explicitamente presente no resumo.

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_topic: The current study investigated whether individual differences in EF could predict individual differences in CIE susceptibility. Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task. The relationship between EF and CIE was then assessed using a correlation analysis of the EF and CIE measures, as well as structural equation modelling of the EF-subcomponent latent variable and CIE latent variable.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando uma tarefa padrão, o que é consistente com o pedido. O estudo é empírico, com participantes humanos, e os resultados sustentam a conclusão de que funções executivas predizem a suscetibilidade ao CIE, conforme descrito no resumo.

items.title: Did he or didn't he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions
judge.reason: O artigo descreve três experimentos com participantes humanos sobre o efeito de influência continuada em cenários fictícios neutros, o que está alinhado com o pedido. O achado extraído é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve quatro experimentos com participantes humanos sobre a influência continuada de desinformação em impressões de pessoas (cenário neutro/fictício), atendendo a todos os critérios do pedido. O achado extraído reflete fielmente o resumo.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE), alinhado ao tema. O resumo confirma os experimentos e os achados principais sobre a colaboração por turnos e livre. O tamanho da amostra não consta no resumo.

items.title: Relative source credibility affects the continued influence effect: Evidence of rationality in the CIE

judge.evidence_topic: Participants read a fictitious news report in which original information and a retraction were each presented by either a source with high credibility or a source with low credibility.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 151, N = 146), informant credibility and retractor credibility were independently manipulated.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (dois experimentos) publicado em periódico revisado por pares (Cognition) que investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando materiais neutros (relatos fictícios). Os dados extraídos refletem corretamente a metodologia e os achados descritos no resumo.

items.title: Combating false information in military situations: Striking the right balance between continued influence effect and overcorrection

judge.evidence_topic: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making
judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making, followed by an assessment of their inferential reasoning.
judge.reason: O artigo utiliza cenários militares, o que viola a restrição de materiais neutros (sem conotação política ou de saúde), pois contextos militares são inerentemente sensíveis e não se enquadram na categoria de cenários fictícios neutros solicitada.

items.title: Failure to accept retractions: A contribution to the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The current study explored whether this effect reflects, at least in part, an unwillingness of some readers to accept changes to their understanding. Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm... Experiment 3 modified the alternative account to increase plausibility, and added two additional stories/question sets to ensure effects were not limited to one set of materials.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiment 1 assessed this using a continued influence effect paradigm... Experiment 2 included an additional explicit instruction... Experiment 3 modified the alternative account...
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada em contextos narrativos neutros, atendendo ao critério de neutralidade. O estudo é empírico, composto por três experimentos, e o método descrito no resumo é consistente com a extração. O achado principal é diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: I know It's false, but I keep thinking as if it were true: A replication study of Johnson and Seifert's (1994) continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.evidence_empirical: The present research investigated the direct replicability of their study with a French-speaking sample, comparing the inferences drawn by an FI group (n = 21) to those made by a control group (n = 23).
judge.reason: O artigo é uma replicação empírica do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando um cenário neutro (referência ao experimento 1A de Johnson e Seifert, que trata de um incêndio em um armazém), atendendo aos critérios de neutralidade e metodologia experimental. O achado está claramente sustentado pelo resumo.
